context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Behold the man; behold your King” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within sentencing.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Flogging, a thorn crown, a purple garment, the pavement, and the judgment seat punctuate the exchange.
observations.label: Behold the man; behold your King: textual observation

observations.body: “The man,” “Son of God,” “king,” and “Caesar” become successive pressure points.
observations.label: Behold the man; behold your King: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Pilate repeatedly goes between Jesus and the accusers before sitting at the pavement and delivering him.
observations.label: Relationships named in John 19:1–16

payload.posture: Read John 19:1–16 as its own sentencing and mockery crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: Pilate repeatedly reports no basis for a charge while fear and political claims intensify toward delivery.
payload.title: Behold the man; behold your King
